events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: The grave is on a hill above a village that still sweeps it every spring. The stone says only a title, the one the whole murim knew. Wind moves the paper streamers on the grave mound. In your sleeve the bell is very cold.

choices.text: Write the talisman and ring the bell

effects.log: You kneel and write in one breath, the brush heavier with every stroke. The village dogs begin to howl before you finish.

choices.text: Leave before the villagers see you

effects.log: You walk back down the hill with the bell muffled in your fist. Some graves are better left to the people who sweep them.

choices.text: Burn incense, and close the grave to yourself for good

effects.log: You light three sticks and bow three times. When you stand up you know you will never come back to this hill.

events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: Nobody tends this grave. The great master died alone in seclusion, and the disciples who carried the coffin down the mountain argued over the manuals until the sect forgot the way here. Mist lies in the hollow of the mound like water in a bowl.

choices.text: Press the yellow talisman into the earth

effects.log: The mist stirs when the paper touches the earth, as if something below had breathed out.

choices.text: Think better of it and go

effects.log: You turn back at the edge of the hollow. All the way down the mountain you feel the grave watching your back.

choices.text: Clear the weeds, and promise the dead their rest

effects.log: You pull the weeds with your hands until the stone can be read again. Then you leave it, and the promise, behind.

events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: A Taoist shrine stands over the grave, and an old keeper sleeps in its doorway with a peachwood sword across his knees. Talismans older than you are pasted on every post. Someone expected this. Someone feared it enough to pay for a keeper for forty years.

choices.text: Step past the sleeping keeper

ok.log: The keeper does not wake. You peel the old talismans from the posts one by one, and the shrine feels larger without them.

fail.log: A floorboard speaks. The keeper is on his feet with the peachwood sword before you can lie, and you leave by the wall.

choices.text: Wake the keeper and ask the way to the gate

effects.log: The old man looks at the bell in your sleeve for a long time, then shows you the road out without a word.

choices.text: Leave a coin for the keeper and go

effects.log: You leave 20 taels in the keeper's bowl and walk away. The shrine will hold, at least while you live.

events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: You know this grave because you made the dead. The mound is small for the name on the stone, and someone has left a cup of wine on it, still full. You remember the last exchange, the look in the eyes, the silence after. The bell in your sleeve rings once by itself.

choices.text: Raise the one you killed

effects.log: You pour the wine out on the earth and write the talisman over the place where it soaked in.

choices.text: Pour out the wine, and walk away

effects.log: The wine smells sour. You pour it on the grass and set the empty cup back on the mound and go, and you do not look back, and it does not help.

choices.text: Kneel, and let the dead keep what you took

effects.log: You kneel until your knees ache, and say nothing, because there is nothing to say. Then you close the grave to yourself for good.

events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: It is the anniversary of the fight, and the grave has visitors: two disciples of the dead master, burning paper money and weeping. They have not seen you yet. Behind the mound the night is waiting, and so is the bell.

choices.text: Wait until they are gone, then raise it

effects.log: You wait in the trees until the last paper money is ash. Then you go down to the grave alone.

choices.text: Leave them their grief

effects.log: You slip back into the dark before the disciples look up. Some nights are not yours.

choices.text: Step out and burn paper money beside them

effects.log: They stare at you, and then, slowly, they make room. Nobody speaks. You will never come here with a bell again.

events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: The bell rings by itself at midnight, three times. When you reach the coffin the lid is on the floor and the Great Jiangshi is standing in the courtyard, facing the road. It is not waiting for your bell. It is remembering the way to somewhere.

choices.text: Ring the bell and hold it with your whole will

ok.log: It turns its head toward the bell, very slowly, and then it walks back to its coffin and lies down. Your arm is numb to the shoulder.

fail.log: It looks at you once, the way a great master looks at a nuisance, and walks out of the gate into the mist.

choices.text: Paste a sealing talisman on its back and lay it down for good

ok.log: The talisman goes on with a slap. The Great Jiangshi falls like a tree, and does not rise again. You bury it before dawn.

fail.log: The talisman tears in the wind of its sleeve. By the time you get up, the courtyard is empty.

choices.text: Let it go where it is going

effects.log: You stand aside. It walks past you without bending its knees, out of the gate, toward the hills it came from.

events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: For a month it has stood a little farther from its coffin each morning. Tonight the talisman on its forehead has gone grey, and the script is fading as you watch. In the village below, someone is ringing a temple bell that is not yours.

choices.text: Write it a new talisman at once

ok.log: Your brush races the fading script and wins by a breath. The new paper burns cold under your palm.

fail.log: The last stroke of the old script fades before you finish the first of the new. The Great Jiangshi is gone before the ink is dry.

choices.text: Walk it back to its grave and lay it to rest

effects.log: You ring the bell one last time and lead it home through the mist, step for step.

choices.text: Do nothing, and see what it does

effects.log: It does what the dead do when nobody holds them. In the morning its coffin is empty and the village bell has stopped.

events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: They come at noon, which is how you know they mean it: a column of the dead master's own sect in mourning white, carrying an empty coffin. Their leader plants a banner at your gate. "We have come to take our elder home. Give back the body, or we take it from yours."

choices.text: Meet them with the Great Jiangshi beside you

ok.log: They break when their old master steps out of your gate toward them. Nobody can raise a sword against that face. They carry the empty coffin away.

fail.log: They fight like people with nothing left to lose. You hold the gate, barely, and the Great Jiangshi strains at the bell all night after.

choices.text: Give the body back to its sect

effects.log: You ring the bell and walk it out to them. The leader weeps openly, and pastes a talisman of their own over yours.

choices.text: Pay them blood money and send them away

effects.log: You pay 500 taels. They take it, which shames them, and go, which shames you. The feud is not over.

events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: A young disciple of the dead master waits at the ferry with a sword far too good for their age. "You dug up my teacher," the disciple says. "I have trained for this every day since." The ferryman has already poled away.

choices.text: Fight the disciple

ok.log: You disarm the disciple and leave them kneeling on the jetty. They will come again, better.

fail.log: The disciple fights with their teacher's own art, and the Great Jiangshi behind you stops moving to watch. You barely get away.

choices.text: Let the disciple see their teacher one last time

effects.log: You ring the bell. The disciple drops the sword and bows to the dead, and the dead, for a moment, almost bows back.

choices.text: Take another ferry

effects.log: You walk three days around the river. Behind you, at every ferry, the disciple asks after you.

events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: The roads are posted with your face now, under a line in red: whoever brings the one who raised a Great from the grave. Tonight a band of righteous swordsmen surrounds the inn where you sleep, with Taoist priests among them and peachwood swords drawn.

choices.text: Break out through the swordsmen

ok.log: You go out through the front door with the Great Jiangshi at your back. Nobody tries the door after the first three.

fail.log: A priest's mirror catches the Great Jiangshi full in the face and it stops dead. You drag it out through the back with your arm on fire.

choices.text: Out over the roofs, and leave the inn behind

effects.log: You leave everything you paid for, 30 taels of it, and go over the roofs into the rain.

choices.text: Surrender the Great Jiangshi to the priests

effects.log: You ring the bell and give it to them. The priests lead it away in silence. The swordsmen let you go, and do not thank you.

events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: A famous Taoist exorcist has sworn on the steps of the provincial temple to lay your Great Jiangshi to rest. People say the exorcist has put down a hundred of the dead. You find the exorcist's lanterns hung across the road ahead, one in every tree.

choices.text: Take the road anyway

ok.log: The lanterns go out one by one as you pass under them. The exorcist is not on the temple steps the next spring.

fail.log: Every lantern you pass under burns the bond a little thinner. You get through, but the Great Jiangshi limps now.

choices.text: Go the long way round, through the marshes

effects.log: A month in the marshes, with leeches and fever. The exorcist waits on the road you never take.

choices.text: Meet the exorcist, and ask for rites

effects.log: The exorcist is younger than you thought, and very tired. Together you walk the dead master home.

events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: You wake to find the Great Jiangshi standing over your bed, perfectly still, in the stance that began the last form of its art. It has never moved without the bell before. The stance is beautiful. It is also aimed at you.

choices.text: Ring the bell, hard

effects.log: It goes back to its coffin at the third ring. In the morning you find your bell cracked down one side.

choices.text: Watch the form to its end

effects.log: It moves through the whole of its last form in the dark, slow as water, and you learn more in one night than in a year.

choices.text: Speak to it by its old title

effects.log: It stops. For a long moment you think it will answer. Then it walks back to its coffin, and lies down, and you do not sleep again.

events.arc: The Great Who Would Not Lie Down
events.text: At the turn of the year the Great Jiangshi stands at the gate all night, facing the direction of its old sect. There is frost on its shoulders in the morning. You find yourself wondering, for the first time, whether it is cold.

choices.text: Lay it to rest before it remembers more

effects.log: You walk it home through the snow. At the grave it lies down before you ask.

choices.text: Bring it inside, and write the talisman thicker

effects.log: You write until your hand cramps. It comes inside when you ring, and the frost melts off it onto your floor.

choices.text: Let it keep its vigil

effects.log: You leave it at the gate. Every new year after, it stands there, a little longer each time.
